I'm 65 this year, and these 8 mu in Quzhou are all the land I have. Twenty years ago I came back to farming — before that I worked in town — so I know both the technical side and the money side. With 10 people in the household and only some of the younger ones earning off-farm wages, cash is always tight. I understand what the extension sheets say about fertilizer rates, but I also know that if I overspend on inputs and the maize price drops or a hailstorm comes, my grandchildren still need to eat. I stay conservative.

**Winter wheat:** I'll plant around October 10th. The soil on my plots is decent loam — not the best in the village, but consistent. I saved seed from last year's plot that yielded well, but I'll mix in about half new improved variety seed to keep vigor up. That comes to roughly 15 kg per mu. For fertilizer, I'm targeting about 13 kg N per mu total. I'll put down a base of compound fertilizer at planting — about 20 kg per mu — and then topdress with urea at jointing in late March, but only if the wheat looks like it can use it. Maybe 10 kg urea per mu. I can't afford the full recommended rate, and I'd rather leave a little yield on the table than run out of cash before maize season. Irrigation is metered and the pump electricity adds up fast. I'll do three times: once right after planting to get germination, once before winter freeze if it's dry, and once at jointing. That's already pushing my water budget. One pass of herbicide in early spring — the weeds here are manageable if you catch them early. We plant by broadcasting and shallow tillage; no time for fancy methods on 8 mu. Family can handle most of it, but I might hire one day of help at harvest when speed matters.

**Summer maize:** The window after wheat harvest is brutal — sometimes six days, sometimes less. I'll hire a combine to cut the wheat, then immediately rotary till and get the maize in by mid-June. No deep tillage possible. Maize seed has to be hybrid — I buy fresh every year, about 3.5 kg per mu. For fertilizer, I'll put all of it at planting: about 12 kg N per mu as compound plus some urea mixed in. No time for split application in this system, and honestly the labor for a second pass is money I don't have. Two irrigations: one after planting if the soil is dry, and one at the big trumpet stage — that's the one that really pays. I'll spray herbicide once and keep an eye for armyworm; if I see them, I'll hit it with insecticide quickly. With 10 people in the house, family labor carries me through most of the season. I might hire two days total — one for planting help and one at harvest — but otherwise we do it ourselves.

My yield target? Last year I got about 420 kg/mu on wheat and 460 on maize. This year I'm hoping for 400 and 450. I'm not greedy. Stability first.
